title: Simplify concurrent snapshot exports
description: An export refactor changes task supervision, publication, and the result reported to callers.
commitMessage: Use gather for snapshot parts and include a part count in export results.
reviewContext: Python 3.11+. One refresh runs at a time; names are unique, nonempty part identifiers. A previously published snapshot must stay readable until a new complete stage is atomically published. Failed work and cancellation must reach the caller. No task may still write to a stage when discard_stage removes it. Store methods have the supplied protocol semantics; discard_stage does not fail. write_part is an async operation that responds to cancellation, not a background thread. Concurrent callers and repeated cancellation during cleanup are outside this exercise.

files.before:
import asyncio
from .store import SnapshotStore


async def refresh_snapshot(store: SnapshotStore, names: list[str]) -> None:
    stage = await store.create_stage()
    try:
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group:
            for name in names:
                group.create_task(store.write_part(stage, name))
        await store.publish(stage)
    except BaseException:
        await store.discard_stage(stage)
        raise
files.after:
import asyncio
from .store import SnapshotStore


async def refresh_snapshot(store: SnapshotStore, names: list[str]) -> None:
    stage = await store.create_stage()
    try:
        await store.clear_current()
        await asyncio.gather(*(store.write_part(stage, name) for name in sorted(names)))
        await store.publish(stage)
    except BaseException:
        await store.discard_stage(stage)
        return
